name: is-the-panels-glass-real
description:
And it re-opens a question already answered for every other surface. The reveal panel is a child NSWindow and installs an NSVisualEffectView with behind-window blending. Four attempts established that a CHILD window does not sample its parent's content: material in the child came back opaque, material in the parent came back sharp, and the only thing seen to frost Chromium output was a TOP-LEVEL window - macOS's own notification banners.

The panel was built after that finding and nobody checked it against a test pattern. If its material contributes nothing, the child window is being paid for with hit-testing, window commands, contents handover and a tracker race, and buying a plain translucent wash that an in-window view could draw.

The reading is the one used for every other surface: a 40px checkerboard of two saturated colours behind the panel. A real frost turns those edges to mush. No frost leaves them crisp.

The pattern reaches the window through the SPACE's own tab, not through `open -a`. An external link opens a LITTLE window here - the log named it, 'external link opened a little window' - and a little window has no sidebar, so the reveal strip stayed on the main window behind it and the collapse chord had nothing to toggle.

actions.note: first paint, and the sidebar announces itself

actions.expression: (() => { const r = document.querySelector('.row'); if (!r) return 'no-row'; r.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: The space's own tab is cold at launch, so the row has to be pressed for the pattern to paint in the MAIN window.

actions.expression: (() => { const b = document.querySelector('.sbtoggle'); if (!b) return 'no-button'; b.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: The row's own Hide button, not Cmd+S. The chord dies whenever an HTML surface holds first responder - the log names the responder as the sidebar's own render widget on both earlier runs, and the pane stayed docked at 244 through each of them. That is a real defect and it has its own task; this reading must not wait on it.

actions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar toggle requested from the chrome row
actions.note: A collapse that never ran leaves the pane docked, and a panel read over a docked pane says nothing about glass.
the collapse animation finishes before anything is read
the checkerboard with no panel over it - the control for what its edges look like unfrosted

Park well inside the page first. The arming strip is 32pt wide measured from the window's CONTENT edge, and the window sits about 8pt from the screen edge, so x=3 was on the desktop and no reveal ever fired - the log's only edge-reveal line came at teardown.
Cross INTO the strip from outside it. A tracking area fires mouseEntered on the crossing, so two points that are both already inside it fire nothing.

actions.pattern: Atrium: sidebar overlay revealing at width
actions.note: the gate: the panel is genuinely up before anything is read off it
the slide finishes, so the capture is of a settled panel rather than a moving one
the panel over the same checkerboard. This frame is the answer and it is read by eye.

assertions.label: the-pattern-was-really-on-screen
assertions.desc: A frame read over a page that never loaded says nothing about frost.

assertions.label: the-panel-covers-the-page-rather-than-showing-it
assertions.desc: The panel draws its own surface in CSS, translucent, so the page reads through it and the rows stay legible. Measured region means: checkerboard alone 127,127,169 - the opaque fill that preceded it 219,222,229, a distance near 145 - a see-through panel 131,130,170, a distance near 5. A wash at .72 lands near 103, so 40 separates a drawn surface from no surface with room on both sides.
